sections.html:
Tax Administration houses two offices. The Real Estate Assessments Office sets values, and Taxpayer Services handles bills and payments.

OfficeWhat it doesHow to reach it
Real Estate Assessments OfficeValues property, answers assessment questions, takes correction requests703-792-6780, realestate@pwcgov.org, 4379 Ridgewood Center Drive, Suite 203, Prince William, VA 22192
Taxpayer ServicesBilling and payment questions703-792-6710, TaxpayerServices@pwcgov.org
Board of EqualizationHears assessment appeals after the office reviewAppeal form posted on the county site

Walk-in hours at the assessment office are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, and phones are staffed from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Pay through the county's Taxpayer Portal. Check washing fraud is the reason the county advises against sending checks in the mail.

Two installments make up the annual bill. Recent notices have set the first half at July 15 and the second at December 5.

Taxpayer Services can confirm this year's exact dates, which is worth doing before you schedule a closing. Owners with mortgages mostly pay through escrow. Servicing companies are billed directly by the county, so a paper bill that lands in your mailbox by mistake should be forwarded to your servicer.

Improvements completed after the year begins can draw a supplemental real estate tax. An addition or a finished basement from the past year is worth asking about.

The formula is simple: assessed value over 100, times the total rate quoted per $100.

Several layers go into that total. Each year the Board of County Supervisors fixes a countywide base rate. Levies for Fire and Rescue and for Mosquito and Forest Pest Management come on top, as do special district levies that fund items like road improvements. Storm water management and solid waste are charged as separate fees. Your address decides which layers apply, so rely on the rate printed on your bill.

  • Look up which special district levies cover your address.
  • Include storm water and solid waste fees when your bill lists them.
  • Ask whether new construction triggers a supplemental bill.

Take it to the Real Estate Assessments Office first. Still unresolved? Next comes the Board of Equalization, and after that the circuit court.

Under the county's Taxpayer Bill of Rights you may look at the working papers behind your value, sit down with assessment staff and request a correction when the value seems wrong or unfair. Your notice and the office can tell you which dates and steps apply.

Va. Code 58.1-3379 sets the ground rules for the board. It presumes the assessor is right, and the burden falls on you to prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, either that the value tops fair market value or that the assessment is not uniform. Evidence of sales and income through the December 31 before the assessment date is allowed.

Va. Code 58.1-3980 offers another path: ask the assessing official to fix an erroneous assessment, within three years after the tax year ends or one year after the assessment, whichever comes later. It addresses mistakes by the assessor, not disputes over opinion of value.

Back tax stays with the property, since the lien outranks all others until paid.

Under Va. Code 58.1-3340, a buyer or foreclosure trustee has to see that sale proceeds go toward every tax assessed on the real estate, with penalties and interest counted. Contract terms divide the year between you and the buyer, and the treasurer or another proper officer then lifts the lien. The closing agent normally pays the balance from your proceeds. Request a payoff from Taxpayer Services that covers the current half, and do it before a closing date is chosen.

A grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of consideration is imposed by Va. Code 58.1-802. Sellers owe it unless the contract assigns it to the buyer, and no deed gets recorded before it is paid. One Circuit Court clerk serves the county, Manassas and Manassas Park, so a single office takes recording questions for all three.

sections.h2: Is your house in the county or a city?
sections.html:
Manassas, the county seat, is an independent city located inside the county, and Manassas Park is another that the county surrounds. Homes in either one get their bills from the city rather than the county. Look at the town named on your deed before searching for a tax account. Confirm the jurisdiction on your bill if you are unsure.

Out west, a green belt known as the rural crescent covers much of the county, and it can affect any parcel bigger than a subdivision lot.

Homeownership is the norm. The 2020 count was 158,525 housing units with 3.0 percent vacant, and 71.6 percent of occupied units were owner-occupied. The market is tied to commuting into Washington, D.C., and to military employers such as Marine Corps Base Quantico.

Owners who are behind, who inherited a house or who face repairs sometimes choose a direct cash sale, which skips repair demands from retail buyers. The lien must still be cleared at closing, so the same payoff steps apply.

Have your parcel or account number and the property address in front of you. If you are asking for a correction, note exactly what you think is wrong, for example the square footage, the finished space or the condition, and gather photos or a contractor's estimate to support it. Staff can only act on specifics. For a billing question, find your most recent bill so the representative can see what has been posted. Emailing first leaves a written record, and the phone line is better for urgent payoff requests.

Allow time for the answer. A request sent the week before closing may not come back before the closing date, so ask early and say plainly that a sale is pending.

Order a payoff from Taxpayer Services covering the current half. See whether recent improvements could produce a supplemental bill. Tell the closing agent which jurisdiction bills the parcel. Read the proration wording so the July 15 and December 5 installments are divided as you expect. Last, ask your servicer how much of the balance escrow already holds, so the payoff and any escrow refund match on the settlement statement. Call each office a few days before closing to confirm that nothing has changed, since a balance can shift when a payment posts or a bill is issued. Bring a photo ID to any in-person visit.

faqs.q: When are Prince William County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Recent notices put the first half at July 15 and the second at December 5. Taxpayer Services can confirm this year's dates.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Prince William County assessment?
faqs.a: The Real Estate Assessments Office at 703-792-6780 or realestate@pwcgov.org. For billing and payment questions, call Taxpayer Services at 703-792-6710.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Prince William County house if I owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, it comes out of your proceeds at closing since the lien has priority. A payoff figure from Taxpayer Services lets the closing agent add penalties and interest correctly.

faqs.q: Does Prince William County bill houses in Manassas?
faqs.a: No. Manassas and Manassas Park are independent cities surrounded by the county and bill their own real estate tax. Confirm the jurisdiction on your deed or bill.

faqs.q: What can I do if I think my Prince William County value is too high?
faqs.a: Request a review from the Real Estate Assessments Office, and if needed appeal to the Board of Equalization or the circuit court. Bring sales or appraisal evidence, because the assessor is presumed correct.
